items.title: Single-credential pools: transient 429/403 benches the only key for 1 hour (no recovery, no fallback)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Summary

When a credential pool has only one usable (non-`DEAD`) entry, a transient throttle benches that sole key for a **full hour**, so single-key / no-fallback setups suffer ~1 hour of hard failures for a throttle that resets in seconds.

### Where

`agent/credential_pool.py`:

```python
EXHAUSTED_TTL_401_SECONDS = 5 * 60      # 5 minutes
EXHAUSTED_TTL_429_SECONDS = 60 * 60     # 1 hour
EXHAUSTED_TTL_DEFAULT_SECONDS = 60 * 60 # 1 hour
```

`_exhausted_ttl()` maps status → TTL with **no awareness of how many credentials the pool has**. The code already special-cases 401 to recover quickly *"so single-key setups can recover"* (the comment is right there), but **429 and the catch-all default (which covers 403/5xx) still get 1 hour even when there is nothing to rotate to.**

### Impact (observed)

Running a single API key (e.g. one Z.AI/GLM coding-plan key, fallbacks removed), a transient `429` (and, from Z.AI's edge, an HTML `403`) trips:

```
credential pool: marking <KEY> exhausted (status=403), rotating
credential pool: no available entries (all exhausted or empty)
API call failed ... error_type=PermissionDeniedError ... HTTP 403
Non-retryable client error
```

The single key is then benched for an hour → every agent on it fails until the TTL expires (or a restart). The throttle itself clears in seconds.

### Proposed fix

When the pool's sole non-`DEAD` entry is exhausted by a **transient** throttle (429 / 403 / 5xx / unknown), cool it down briefly instead of an hour — mirroring the existing 401 single-key rationale. Keep the full bench for `402` (billing/quota), where a quick retry can't help, and continue to honor provider-supplied `reset_at`.

PR with fix + tests attached.

items.title: Knowledge: Three undocumented gateway modes cause inconsistent terminal CWD behaviour on Windows

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes has three distinct operational modes for session initialization, but none are documented — not in `website/docs/`, not in code comments, not in any issue or PR. Users and contributors cannot understand why tool behavior differs between `hermes` (CLI), `hermes gateway start` (full gateway), and the Desktop/TUI (embedded gateway).

The three modes resolve the terminal working directory (`TERMINAL_CWD`) differently, which directly impacts Windows path conversion and terminal tool reliability.

## Three Modes (Reverse-Engineered from Source)

### 1. Plain CLI — `hermes chat --no-tui`

- No gateway process — agent runs in-process
- `cli.py:583`: `terminal_config["cwd"] = os.getcwd()` → Windows native format
- `_HERMES_GATEWAY` NOT set

### 2. Embedded Gateway (TUI / Desktop) — `hermes` (default)

- TUI spawns a Pty child hermes subprocess
- `HERMES_CWD = os.getcwd()` at TUI launch → `TERMINAL_CWD` = Windows native format
- Not the full multi-channel gateway — single-channel embedded server

### 3. Full Gateway — `hermes gateway start`

- Dedicated gateway process with multi-channel dispatch
- `gateway/run.py:1426`: `TERMINAL_CWD` falls back to `os.path.expanduser("~")` → MSYS format
- `_HERMES_GATEWAY=1` — prevents `cli.py` from overwriting

## Why This Matters for Windows Users

Modes 1 & 2 pass `os.getcwd()` (Windows native `C:\Users\...`) through to bash `cd` commands. Git Bash cannot parse drive-letter paths inside single-quoted strings. PR #50596 added `_windows_to_msys_path()` to convert these, but **live sessions have been observed to fail** even with the fix, while the same path works in direct testing — suggesting an unidentified environment variable interaction in the subprocess environment.

Mode 3 (Full Gateway) is unaffected because `os.path.expanduser("~")` already produces MSYS-compatible paths.

## Temporary Workaround

Users hitting terminal tool failures (`exit_code: 126`, `cd: /c/Users/...: No such file or directory`) can start the full gateway first and reload the conversation:

```
hermes gateway start
```

Then restart or reload the session. The Full Gateway resolves CWD through `os.path.expanduser("~")` which produces bash-compatible paths on MSYS Git Bash.

## Request

1. **Documentation:** Confirm or correct the three-mode architecture described above. A `docs/architecture/gateway-modes.md` would help users and contributors.

2. **Root cause:** The live-session terminal failure under `_windows_to_msys_path()` — unit tests pass but live CLI/Embedded sessions can still break. Suspected factors: `HOME` override via `get_subprocess_home()`, `TERMINAL_HOME_MODE` interaction, or stale `_active_environments` cache.

3. **Centralized fix:** Consider normalizing `TERMINAL_CWD` at the bridge layer (`cli.py:583`) instead of in `base.py` — `_windows_to_msys_path(os.getcwd())` would eliminate the gap between all three modes.

## Disclaimer

All architectural conclusions above are derived from source code analysis of `hermes_cli/main.py`, `cli.py`, `gateway/run.py`, `tools/terminal_tool.py`, and `tools/environments/base.py`. They have not been confirmed by the Hermes maintainers. Correction or supplementation from the core team is welcome.

## Bug Description

Hermes subprocess calls on Windows flash black `cmd.exe` windows. This happens whenever the agent uses the terminal tool, gateway runs housekeeping/cron jobs, or internal subprocesses are spawned. The flashing makes the desktop app nearly unusable — windows appear and disappear every few seconds.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes Desktop on Windows 10/11
2. Start the gateway
3. Use any feature that spawns subprocesses (terminal tool, gateway housekeeping, cron jobs)
4. Observe black `cmd.exe` windows flashing on screen

## Expected Behavior

All subprocess calls should run silently in the background on Windows. No visible console windows should appear.

## Actual Behavior

`cmd.exe` windows flash on screen whenever subprocesses are spawned. This includes:
- Agent's `terminal` tool (every shell command)
- Gateway housekeeping (every 60 seconds)
- Cron job execution
- Internal process spawning

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes: Desktop (Electron)
- Gateway: running with Weixin platform adapter

## Likely Root Cause

Subprocess calls on Windows are not passing `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` / `windowsHide: true` consistently. In Node.js this is `{ windowsHide: true }` on `spawn()`/`exec()`, in Python `subprocess.STARTUPINFO(dwFlags=subprocess.STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW, wShowWindow=subprocess.SW_HIDE)`.

## Impact

High — makes the desktop app frustrating to use on Windows, the primary platform for many users.

items.body:
## Problem

The Hermes Agent system prompt contains a static `Conversation started: <day>, <month> <day>, <year>` line (no time-of-day, no timezone). This timestamp is captured at session start and never refreshed.

When the session spans a timezone change, a date rollover, or the agent needs to reason about "how long until X" or "when did Y happen" relative to the conversation, the agent can produce confidently wrong answers.

## Concrete repro (observed today, 2026-06-26)

User asked when F1 FP1 starts in Austria (13:30 CEST per the F1 schedule).

The NAS system clock correctly showed **14:04 CEST** (verified via `date`, `python3 datetime.now()`, and `chrony` synced to `time.google.com`).

The agent calculated "~ 11:20 NL-tijd, dus over ~2 uur" — **wrong by ~3 hours**. FP1 was already 34 minutes into the session when the agent said it was "a few hours away".

The system prompt at the top of this conversation said only:
```
Conversation started: Friday, June 26, 2026
```
which matches today's date but gives **no time-of-day or timezone**. The agent had no machine-readable anchor to sanity-check its own arithmetic.

## Expected

The agent should be able to say "FP1 started 34 minutes ago, it ends in ~26 minutes" without doing mental math against a vague date string.

## Suggested fixes (any one of these would solve it)

1. **Add a live clock** to every turn: include `Current time (UTC): 2026-06-26T12:04:36Z` and `Local time (Europe/Amsterdam): 2026-06-26T14:04:36+02:00` in the system prompt or as a per-turn user-context line. The model already has datetime reasoning; it just needs an anchor it can trust.

2. **Replace the static `Conversation started` line** with `Conversation started: 2026-06-26T13:55:12+02:00` (ISO 8601 with offset). Models parse this reliably.

3. **Expose a `current_time` tool** so the agent can `call current_time()` whenever it needs an authoritative timestamp — like the built-in `date` tool, but explicit and documented as the single source of truth for "now".

Option 1 is the cheapest and most reliable: every model already knows how to use ISO 8601 in context, and there's no new tool surface.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (NousResearch/hermes-agent), running on Synology NAS DSM 7.3
- Model: MiniMax-M3 (per user config)
- System clock: verified correct via `chrony` synced to `time.google.com`
- Python: 3.8.15, no NTP errors, `datetime.now()` returns correct local time

## Severity

Medium — wrong relative-time answers erode user trust quickly, especially in time-sensitive domains (sports, markets, appointments). Doesn't break functionality but actively misleads.

items.title: delegation.provider=custom:* resolves wrong base_url (inherits parent provider base_url)
items.body:
# Bug Report: delegation.provider=custom:* resolves wrong base_url (inherits parent provider base_url instead of custom provider config)

**Hermes Version:** v0.17.0
**OS:** macOS 26.5.1
**Python:** 3.11

## Description

When `delegation.provider` is set to a `custom:*` provider, subagents correctly receive the provider name (`custom:or-api`) and the model override, but `resolve_runtime_provider()` returns the **parent agent's base_url** instead of the custom provider's configured `base_url`. This causes the subagent to send API calls to the wrong endpoint, which fails (503 or model_not_found), triggering the fallback chain that routes everything back to the parent's provider.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a custom provider in `config.yaml`:
```yaml
custom_providers:
- name: or-api
  base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
  api_mode: chat_completions
  key_env: OR_API_KEY
  model: anthropic/claude-opus-4.8
```

2. Set delegation config:
```yaml
delegation:
  provider: custom:or-api
  model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
```

3. Run any `delegate_task` without explicit model/provider parameters.

## Expected Behavior

- Subagent uses `provider=custom:or-api`, `base_url=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, `model=anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`
- `billing_provider` in state.db = `custom:or-api`

## Actual Behavior

- Subagent gets `provider=custom:or-api` BUT `base_url=https://www.micuapi.ai` (parent agent's default provider URL)
- API call fails: `HTTP 503: No available channel for model deepseek/deepseek-chat`
- Fallback chain activates → subagent ends up on `custom:micu-gpt` / `gpt-5.5`
- `billing_provider` in state.db = `custom:micu-gpt`
- All subsequent subagents skip `custom:or-api` entirely (fallback pool exhaustion)

## Evidence

### state.db (10 consecutive subagent sessions)
```
20260626_200120_ca8207 | anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 | custom:micu-gpt
20260626_200243_d0c92a | deepseek/deepseek-chat     | custom:micu-gpt
20260626_200429_c28b62 | claude-sonnet-4-6          | custom:micu-gpt
20260626_200518_485e14 | claude-sonnet-4-6          | custom:micu-gpt
... (all 10 show custom:micu-gpt)
```

### agent.log (the ONLY session that tried custom:or-api)
```
session=20260626_200243_d0c92a provider=custom:or-api base_url=https://www.micuapi.ai model=deepseek/deepseek-chat

# Then fails:
API call failed (attempt 1/3) provider=custom:or-api base_url=https://www.micuapi.ai model=deepseek/deepseek-chat
summary=HTTP 503: No available channel for model deepseek/deepseek-chat

# Then fallback:
Fallback to custom:micu-claude/claude-opus-4.8: clearing primary credential pool (pool_provider=custom:or-api)
Fallback activated: anthropic/claude-opus-4.8 → gpt-5.5 (custom:micu-gpt)
```

Note: `base_url` is `https://www.micuapi.ai` but custom provider config says `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`.

### Later subagent sessions — OR never attempted again
```
# All subsequent sessions go straight to micu-gpt:
Fallback activated: anthropic/claude-opus-4.8 → gpt-5.5 (custom:micu-gpt)
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The bug is in `resolve_runtime_provider()` called from `_resolve_delegation_credentials()` (line 2823 of `tools/delegate_tool.py`):

```python
runtime = resolve_runtime_provider(requested=configured_provider, target_model=configured_model)
```

For `requested="custom:or-api"`, this function resolves the provider name correctly but returns the **parent agent's `base_url`** instead of the custom provider's configured `base_url`. This suggests the custom provider lookup is either:
1. Falling through to the default/parent provider for fields not explicitly set
2. Not correctly matching the "or-api" name after stripping the "custom:" prefix
3. Not loading the `custom_providers` section from config in the delegation context

The custom provider config is correct and works for first-level calls (`hermes chat --provider custom:or-api` works fine). The bug only manifests in the delegation subagent path.

## Related Issues

- #10653 — delegation.provider ignored (fixed in PR #16329, but may have regressed)
- #16816 — ACP transport leak bypasses delegation.provider (fixed in #16894)
- #17685 — per-task model override silently ignored (open, PR in progress)
- #26482 — delegation model override ignored, claimed "fixed on main" but follow-up reports (#26722, #27294-27296) indicate regression

This bug is a **new variant**: provider name IS passed correctly, but base_url resolution for `custom:*` providers is wrong in the delegation path.

## Workaround

None clean. The `custom:or-api` provider works for first-level calls but not for subagents. Using `delegation.base_url` + `delegation.api_key` directly (bypassing the provider name resolution) may work but hasn't been tested.

## Labels

`type/bug` `P2` `tool/delegate` `comp/agent` `area/config` `regression`

items.body:
## Summary

Two Windows-specific bugs make Hermes Desktop nearly unusable on non-English (especially Chinese) Windows:

1. **Bug A: Backend crash loop** — Desktop stuck on "Connecting…" forever because the Python backend crashes with `UnicodeDecodeError` on GBK-encoded subprocess output
2. **Bug B: Terminal window flood** — When the AI runs shell commands, each one spawns a visible console window that flickers and steals focus

Both have simple, safe one-line fixes.

---

## Bug A: GBK encoding crash loop → Desktop can't start

### Root Cause

When the Desktop spawns the Python backend, it doesn't set `PYTHONUTF8=1`. On Windows, Python defaults to the **system locale code page** for subprocess pipe I/O — on Chinese Windows this is **GBK (CP936)**.

When the backend spawns subprocesses whose stdout/stderr contain bytes invalid in that code page (ANSI escapes, Unicode box-drawing, binary tool output), Python's internal `subprocess._readerthread` raises:

```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x94 in position 30: illegal multibyte sequence
```

This kills the backend. Desktop respawns it → same crash → loops forever.

### Where

- `apps/desktop/electron/backend-env.cjs` — `buildDesktopBackendEnv()` (covers `createActiveBackend` / `createPythonBackend`)
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` — two inline `spawn()` calls (belt-and-suspenders for the `env: {}` fallback paths)

### Fix

```diff
// backend-env.cjs — buildDesktopBackendEnv return value
+ PYTHONUTF8: '1',

// main.cjs — both spawn() env objects
+ PYTHONUTF8: '1',
```

[PEP 540](https://peps.python.org/pep-0540/) UTF-8 Mode is safe on all platforms and already standard in CI/containers.

### Logs

```
[hermes] [gateway-crash] thread Thread-216 (_readerthread) raised UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x94 in position 30: illegal multibyte sequence
[hermes] Hermes backend exited (3221226091)
[hermes] [boot] Hermes backend exited before it became ready (3221226091).
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes backend exited before it became ready (3221226091).
```

---

## Bug B: Terminal window flood when AI runs shell commands

### Root Cause

`tools/environments/local.py` `_run_bash()` sets `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` via `windows_hide_flags()`, which hides the **direct child** (`bash.exe`). But when Git Bash (MSYS2) internally spawns native Windows programs (`git.exe`, `python.exe`, `node.exe`, etc.), those grandchildren find no console allocated and **each creates its own visible window**.

`CREATE_NO_WINDOW` alone doesn't propagate to grandchildren. The fix requires `STARTUPINFO.dwFlags |= STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW` + `wShowWindow = SW_HIDE`, which tells the Windows kernel to suppress windows for the **entire process tree**.

### Where

`tools/environments/local.py` — `_run_bash()` method.

### Fix

```diff
- _popen_kwargs = {"creationflags": windows_hide_flags()} if _IS_WINDOWS else {}
+ if _IS_WINDOWS:
+     _startupinfo = subprocess.STARTUPINFO()
+     _startupinfo.dwFlags |= subprocess.STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW
+     _startupinfo.wShowWindow = subprocess.SW_HIDE
+     _popen_kwargs = {"creationflags": windows_hide_flags(), "startupinfo": _startupinfo}
+ else:
+     _popen_kwargs = {}
```

---

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro (Chinese locale, code page GBK/CP936)
- Hermes Desktop built from `e3db1ef`
- Node 22.x, Python 3.11 (uv-managed venv)
- Git for Windows (bash.exe at `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\bash.exe`)

items.body:
### Bug Description

## Summary
For cron jobs with `no_agent: true`, the per-job `profile` field is **not applied** before the script runs. The script (and its `scripts/` directory) is resolved under **whichever gateway process happens to win the tick**, not under the job's configured profile. In a multi-gateway / multi-profile setup this makes a profile-scoped `no_agent` job fail (or run under the wrong profile's environment) non-deterministically.

Agent-backed jobs (`no_agent: false`) are unaffected — they get correct profile scoping.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent **v0.17.0**, built-in cron provider (`cron.provider` empty)
- More than one gateway running under different profiles, all sharing the root cron store (`$HERMES_ROOT/cron/jobs.json`)

## Severity
Medium. Silent / non-deterministic failure of scheduled `no_agent` jobs whenever more than one gateway is running. The job's documented `--profile` scoping (creds/config/env) is also silently not applied even when the script *is* found.




### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run two gateways under different profiles:
   - `hermes --profile A gateway run`
   - `hermes --profile B gateway run`
2. Create a `no_agent` cron job whose script lives in profile **B**'s scripts dir and is scoped to B:
   ```
   hermes cron create '*/15 * * * *' --name demo \
     --script my_script.py --no-agent \
     --workdir <HERMES_ROOT>/profiles/B \
     --profile B
   ```
   (`<HERMES_ROOT>/profiles/B/scripts/my_script.py` exists; the root `<HERMES_ROOT>/scripts/` does **not** contain it.)
3. Wait for scheduled ticks. Do **not** use `hermes cron run` from the default context — that masks the bug because it ticks under the root home.

### Expected Behavior

The job runs under profile **B**: `HERMES_HOME` is set to B before the script resolves, so `profiles/B/scripts/my_script.py` is found and executes with B's `.env` / config — regardless of which gateway claimed the tick.

### Actual Behavior

The script is resolved under the **ticking gateway's** home. When gateway **A** wins the tick:
```
ERROR cron.scheduler: Job 'demo' failed:
Script not found: <HERMES_ROOT>/profiles/A/scripts/my_script.py
```
The job's `profile: B` is never applied on the `no_agent` path. Which gateway wins is a race (shared root `.tick.lock`), so the failing path/home varies tick to tick.

### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/B3xwC
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/jcuWP
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/RzLCU
  gui.log      https://paste.rs/5Clma
```

### Operating System

mac os

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)


## Root cause
`cron/scheduler.py`, function `run_job` (def ~line 1605). Two relevant blocks, in execution order:

- **~line 1633** — `no_agent` short-circuit runs the script immediately and returns:
  ```python
  if job.get("no_agent"):
      script_path = job.get("script")
      ...
      ok, output = _run_job_script(script_path)   # runs here
      ...
      return ...                                   # no_agent returns before profile scoping
  ```
- **~line 1735** — profile→HERMES_HOME scoping, which a `no_agent` job has *already returned before reaching*:
  ```python
  # Scope this job's execution to its owning profile's HERMES_HOME BEFORE
  # any prompt/skill loading or pre-run script execution...
  os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = str(_profile_home)
  ```

`_run_job_script` (def ~line 1184) resolves the script against `_get_hermes_home() / "scripts"` and enforces it stays inside that dir (path-traversal / symlink-escape guard). Because the no_agent path runs *before* the HERMES_HOME override, `_get_hermes_home()` returns the ticker's home, not the job's profile.

The comment above the override explicitly states it must happen *"BEFORE any prompt/skill loading or pre-run script execution"* so a job doesn't *"resolve scripts/skills from whichever profile's ticker happened to pick it up."* But the `no_agent` short-circuit sits **above** that override and hits exactly the failure the comment is trying to prevent.

## Suggested fix
Hoist the profile→HERMES_HOME scoping **above** the `no_agent` short-circuit, so both the no_agent script path and the agent path resolve under the job's profile. Make sure the `HERMES_HOME` override is restored (e.g. via `finally`) on the no_agent early-return as well.

## Workaround (no code change)
Use a thin shim placed as a **real file** (not a symlink — the path-safety guard blocks symlinks that escape the scripts dir) in **every** running gateway's `scripts/` dir, that sets the target home itself:
```python
import os, runpy
h = "<HERMES_ROOT>/profiles/B"
os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = h
os.chdir(h)
runpy.run_path(h + "/scripts/my_script.py", run_name="__main__")
```
Point the job's `--script` at the shim. Because any gateway can claim the tick, the shim must exist under each gateway home's `scripts/`.

## Notes
- `--workdir` *is* honored on the no_agent path (sets the subprocess cwd), but cwd does not affect script *resolution*, which is anchored to `HERMES_HOME/scripts`.
- Absolute `--script` paths don't bypass this: `_run_job_script` still requires the resolved path to live inside `HERMES_HOME/scripts`.

items.body:
## Summary

The Desktop statusbar version pill shows the commit-behind count (e.g. `v0.17.0 (+28)`), but after a restart it only shows the version number with no counter. The counter only appears after the user manually clicks the version pill to open the updates overlay.

## Root Cause

`startUpdatePoller()` in `src/store/updates.ts` only calls `checkBackendUpdates()` — it never calls `checkUpdates()` (the client/local update check):

```typescript
// store/updates.ts — startUpdatePoller()
backgroundTimer = setInterval(() => {
  void checkBackendUpdates()  // ← only backend!
}, 30 * 60 * 1000)
```

The statusbar `clientVersionItem` reads `` (set by `checkUpdates()`), not ``. Since `checkUpdates()` is never auto-triggered, `` stays `null` → `behind` defaults to 0 → no counter shown.

For local-mode Desktop (gateway runs on same machine), `checkBackendUpdates()` early-returns because `isRemoteMode() === false`, so even the background timer does nothing.

## Expected

The version pill automatically shows the commit-behind count shortly after launch, without requiring the user to click it.

## Actual

- Version pill shows only `v0.17.0` (no `(+N)`)
- Counter only appears after clicking the pill (which triggers `checkUpdates()` → `bridge.check()` → `git fetch` → count)

## Suggestion

`startUpdatePoller()` should also call `checkUpdates()` on startup and include it in the periodic timer / focus handler:

```typescript
export function startUpdatePoller(): void {
  // ...
  void checkUpdates()        // ← add client check
  void checkBackendUpdates()
  // ...
  backgroundTimer = setInterval(() => {
    void checkUpdates()      // ← add client check
    void checkBackendUpdates()
  }, 30 * 60 * 1000)
}
```

And `onFocus` should also trigger `checkUpdates()`.

items.body:
Labels: **enhancement**

**Problem**
When using Hermes Desktop (or any API server client) connected to a remote gateway, each client sends its own model field in the API payload. The gateway passes it through, so the client's model selection wins — even when the server's config.yaml has a deliberate model.default configured.

In a single-user homelab setup (one server, one config, multiple devices), this is surprising:

- Server config.yaml: model.default: qwen3.5-64k (custom Ollama provider)
- Terminal on server: correctly uses qwen3.5-64k
- Hermes Desktop on a Mac: cached a different model (z-ai/glm-5.2 via Nous provider) locally, sends it to the gateway, and the gateway serves it without question

The user expects model.default to be authoritative for all Hermes surfaces. Restarting the server doesn't help because the client's cached preference persists on the client device.

**Current behavior**
The API server is stateless per-request and honors the client's model field. This is correct for third-party clients (Open WebUI, LobeChat, etc.) and matches the OpenAI API convention.

**Proposed solution**
Add a config option:

``` yaml
model:
  force_default: true
```

When enabled, the API server ignores the client's model field and always uses model.default (with model.provider, model.base_url, model.api_key) from the server's config.

- Default: false (preserves current behavior, backward compatible)
- When true: all API server clients — including Hermes Desktop — are forced to the server's configured model
- Third-party clients that send a different model name get the server's model anyway (the response's model field reflects the actual model used)

**Why this matters**

- Single-user homelabs: one server, one config, multiple devices. Centralized control is expected.
- Cost/provider management: the server owner may have intentionally configured a local Ollama model to avoid API costs. A desktop client silently switching to a paid provider defeats that.
- Consistency: the terminal and desktop should not behave differently when talking to the same gateway.

**Alternatives considered**
- Manually setting the model on every client device — fragile, doesn't scale, clients can change it back
- Blocking models at the provider level — overly complex for a simple "use what the server says" need
- Not using Hermes Desktop — defeats the purpose

### Bug Description

On Windows, Hermes installer fails at the `desktop` stage while installing desktop workspace npm dependencies. The failing command is `npm ci` in the repository root; the installer then retries with `npm install`, but the same esbuild postinstall failure occurs.

The exact npm error is:

```text
Error: Expected 0.28.1 but got 0.27.7
    at validateBinaryVersion (C:\Users\zhouy\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\node_modules\esbuild\install.js:137:11)
    at C:\Users\zhouy\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\node_modules\esbuild\install.js:296:5

Node.js v22.22.2
npm error code 1
npm error path C:\Users\zhouy\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\node_modules\esbuild
npm error command failed
npm error command C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /d /s /c node install.js
```

Installer-level failure:

```text
bootstrap FAILED stage=Some(desktop) error=desktop workspace npm install failed (exit 1) -- see lines above for cause
```

This looks related to, but more specific than:

- #46260 (`desktop workspace npm install failed` on Windows installer)
- #37934 (Windows esbuild host/binary mismatch)
- #44121 (`npm ci` / lockfile drift around platform packages)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a clean Hermes checkout from `main`.
2. Ensure `package-lock.json` is unmodified.
3. On Windows, run:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\zhouy\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent
git restore -- package-lock.json
npm ci --foreground-scripts
```

4. Observe `esbuild@0.28.1 postinstall` failing with `Expected 0.28.1 but got 0.27.7`.

The same failure also happens through the GUI installer at step 9/16, `Building desktop app`.

### Expected Behavior

`npm ci` should install the committed lockfile successfully on Windows and the installer should proceed past the desktop dependency install/build stage.

### Actual Behavior

`npm ci` fails during `esbuild@0.28.1` postinstall because the JS package expects `0.28.1`, but the binary that runs reports `0.27.7`.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation, Desktop app, Windows

### Debug Report

```shell
OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
Node.js: v22.22.2
npm: 11.17.0
Python: 3.11.15
Repository: NousResearch/hermes-agent
Branch: main
HEAD: 8ab7246c45383cfcda4944d3872efa56f515f87f
Working tree before reproduction: clean
```

### Additional Logs / Traceback

Before running `npm ci`, inspecting the committed `package-lock.json` shows that `esbuild@0.28.1` is present, but platform package entries are missing:

```text
optional @esbuild entries: 0
win32-x64: MISSING
```

The `node_modules/esbuild` package entry declares optional dependencies such as:

```json
optionalDependencies: {
  @esbuild/win32-arm64: 0.28.1,
  @esbuild/win32-ia32: 0.28.1,
  @esbuild/win32-x64: 0.28.1
}
```

However, the lockfile does not contain corresponding `packages` entries like:

```text
node_modules/@esbuild/win32-x64
```

In a fresh temporary test project, `npm install esbuild@0.28.1` does generate the expected `node_modules/@esbuild/win32-x64` lockfile entry, and `node_modules/esbuild/bin/esbuild.exe --version` returns `0.28.1`.

### Root Cause Analysis

The committed lockfile appears incomplete for esbuild's optional platform binary packages. On Windows, `npm ci` installs `esbuild@0.28.1` but does not install the matching `@esbuild/win32-x64@0.28.1` platform package because that package is absent from `package-lock.json`'s `packages` section. `esbuild` then falls back during postinstall and ends up executing/downloading a mismatched `0.27.7` binary, causing the version validation failure.

I verified a local workaround:

1. Generate a normal lockfile in a temp project with `npm install esbuild@0.28.1`.
2. Copy the 26 `node_modules/@esbuild/*` package entries into Hermes `package-lock.json`.
3. Re-run:

```powershell
npm ci --foreground-scripts
npm run pack --workspace apps/desktop
```

Both commands then complete successfully, and `node_modules/esbuild/bin/esbuild.exe --version` reports `0.28.1`.

### Proposed Fix

Regenerate and commit `package-lock.json` so the `@esbuild/*@0.28.1` optional platform package entries are present, especially `node_modules/@esbuild/win32-x64` for Windows x64.

It may also be worth adding a CI check that runs `npm ci` on Windows with the current supported npm version, because this failure reproduces before any Hermes code runs.

---
title: "v0.17.0: Sidebar empty after restart — Electron cannot discover dashboard random port"
---

## Summary

After updating to Hermes Desktop v0.17.0, the sidebar shows no sessions even though `state.db` contains 50+ sessions. The dashboard process starts with `--port 0` (random port), writes `HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY port=X` to stdout, but the Electron main process fails to parse and relay this port to the renderer. The renderer then attempts API calls on an old/stale port, gets connection refused, and renders an empty sidebar.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Update to Hermes Desktop v0.17.0
2. Restart the desktop application
3. Observe: left sidebar (session list) is empty
4. Existing sessions (50 in `state.db`) are not visible

## Expected Behavior

The sidebar should populate with recent sessions from `state.db` via the dashboard API, regardless of which random port the dashboard binds to.

## Actual Behavior

- Sidebar is empty (no sessions shown)
- Console shows repeated errors: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'refText')` (17+ occurrences in desktop.log)
- Dashboard is running on a random port (e.g., 49720), but the renderer tries to connect to an old port (e.g., 60764)
- Direct API call to the correct dashboard port works: `curl http://127.0.0.1:49720/api/profiles/sessions` returns `{"detail":"Unauthorized"}` (server is alive)
- Direct API call to the stale port fails: `curl http://127.0.0.1:60764/api/profiles/sessions` → `Connection refused`

## Technical Details

### Environment
- **Version:** Hermes Desktop v0.17.0 (build from 2026-06-26)
- **OS:** macOS (26.5.1, Apple Silicon / arm64)
- **Python:** 3.11.15 (in venv at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv`)
- **Profile:** `default`
- **Projects:** `second-brain` (Obsidian vault)

### Process State
```
Dashboard:    PID 46329 — python -m hermes_cli.main dashboard --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
Gateway:      PID 99471 — python -m hermes_cli.main gateway restart
Slash Worker: PID 46379 — tui_gateway.slash_worker (session 20260626_164246)
```

### Dashboard Port History (from desktop.log)
Each restart picks a new random port — the renderer never receives the current one:
```
port=51605 → 49600 → 49719 → 50392 → 50612 → 60551 → 62887 → 64580 → 64603 → 55320 → 55404 → 51610 → 51710 → 50587 → 49547 → 50233 → 51820 → 63616 → 55735 → 60764 → 49720
```

### Data Integrity
- `state.db` contains 50 sessions — data is **not lost**
- `sessions.json` contains only active gateway sessions (Telegram DM) — by design per v0.17.0 docs
- The problem is purely the **UI rendering path** — the renderer cannot reach the dashboard API

### Console Errors (renderer)
```
[hermes] [renderer console] Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'refText')
(file:///Users/alyaschenko/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-DMtH-kyj.js:75)
```
17 occurrences across multiple JS bundles (index-DMtH-kyj.js, index-BHJ4aQFM.js).

### API Verification
```bash
# Correct port (49720) — server responds:
$ curl http://127.0.0.1:49720/api/profiles/sessions?limit=3
{"detail":"Unauthorized"}  # ← server is alive, just needs auth

# Stale port (60764) — connection refused:
$ curl http://127.0.0.1:60764/api/profiles/sessions?limit=3
Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 60764: Couldn't connect to server
```

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The dashboard process starts with `--port 0` (random port assignment). It writes `HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY port=X` to stdout. The Electron main process should:

1. Parse this stdout line
2. Extract the port number
3. Pass it to the renderer via `window.hermesDesktop` (or equivalent IPC channel)
4. The renderer then uses this URL for all API calls

**Post-v0.17.0, step 3 is broken.** The main process either:
- Fails to parse the `HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY` message, OR
- Parses it but fails to relay it to the renderer IPC layer, OR
- The renderer has a hardcoded/stale port from a previous session

The `refText` TypeError in the renderer (line 75 of bundled JS) may be a secondary symptom — possibly caused by an undefined config object when the dashboard URL is missing.

## Relevant Code Paths (from source)

- `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts` — API client (`listAllProfileSessions` calls `/api/profiles/sessions`)
- `apps/desktop/src/app/desktop-controller.tsx` — `refreshSessions()` calls `listAllProfileSessions(limit, 1, 'exclude', 'recent', sessionProfile, { excludeSources: SIDEBAR_EXCLUDED_SOURCES })`
- `apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts` — `$sessions` atom (appears empty)

The dashboard config in `config.yaml` shows:
```yaml
dashboard:
  theme: default
  show_token_analytics: false
  oauth:
    client_id: ''
    portal_url: ''
  basic_auth:
    username: ''
    password_hash: ''
```

No `public_url` or hardcoded dashboard URL is configured — the system relies entirely on runtime port discovery.

## Impact

- **All sessions hidden** in sidebar after any restart/reload
- **Current session invisible** — even the active conversation is not shown
- **No workaround** available without modifying compiled JS bundles in `app.asar`
- **Data is safe** — `state.db` is intact, this is purely a UI routing issue

## Suggested Fix Direction

1. Ensure the Electron main process correctly parses `HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY port=X` from dashboard stdout
2. Ensure this port is relayed to the renderer via IPC (`window.hermesDesktop` or equivalent)
3. Ensure the renderer uses the dynamic port for all API calls (not a hardcoded/stale one)
4. Add error handling: if dashboard is unreachable, show a clear error message instead of silently empty sidebar
5. Consider adding a `dashboard.public_url` config option as a fallback (current config schema already has this field, but it may not be wired up)

## Logs Available

Full `desktop.log` and `gateway.log` available in `~/.hermes/logs/`.

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway hangs after graceful shutdown — sys.exit(1) blocks on stuck non-daemon tool-worker thread (needs os._exit backstop)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

The gateway can hang **after its graceful shutdown has already completed**. On `SIGTERM`, `start_gateway()` runs the full teardown (all platform adapters disconnect, sessions saved, cron ticker stopped, MCP closed) and returns, then `main()` calls `sys.exit(1)`. But `sys.exit()` raises `SystemExit`, and CPython's interpreter finalization (`Py_FinalizeEx` → `wait_for_thread_shutdown`) **blocks until every non-daemon thread joins**. If a `ThreadPoolExecutor` tool-worker is stuck on a no-timeout operation (e.g. an in-flight LLM/tool HTTP call over a degraded link), the process never exits.

Because the adapters are *already torn down* at that point, the result is: api_server is down, Discord/Slack disconnected, and the cron ticker stopped — but the process lingers, so the supervisor (s6 here; systemd elsewhere) does not start a replacement. The gateway is effectively dead while appearing "up", until something force-kills it. Observed hang times ranged from ~2 minutes to indefinite (cleared only by `SIGKILL`).

A downstream consequence: an interval cron job scheduled during the hang window is missed, and its `next_run_at` is left stranded in the past; the ticker does not catch up past-due jobs, so the job silently stops firing until manually re-armed.

### Not a duplicate of the related shutdown issues — distinct phase

This is a *different root cause* from the existing gateway shutdown-hang reports, and the fix is complementary:

- **#14128** (`adapter.disconnect()` without timeout) — hang is in the **disconnect phase**. In our case disconnect completes cleanly in <0.5s; the hang is **after** teardown, in interpreter finalization.
- **#27563** (CLOSED, comp/cli) — *same underlying mechanism* (a worker thread blocks `Py_FinalizeEx`), but reported for the CLI/`prompt_toolkit` path and closed without a fix. This issue is the **gateway** manifestation, triggered by a tool-worker thread.
- **#37454** (orphan child process blocks cgroup cleanup) and **#37763** (cron-child SIGTERM coupling) are adjacent but about *child* processes / signal sourcing, not the gateway's own interpreter hang.

A single force-exit backstop after graceful shutdown (below) would make the whole family of "teardown finished but the process won't die" cases non-fatal, regardless of which thread is stuck.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes gateway run` under a process supervisor (s6 / systemd).
2. Start an agent turn (or cron job) that issues a tool/LLM call which blocks with no effective timeout (a flaky/slow upstream reliably reproduces; the worker runs in the shared `ThreadPoolExecutor`).
3. While that worker is in-flight, send `SIGTERM` (e.g. `s6-svc -r`, `systemctl restart`, or any external `kill`).
4. Observe: the graceful-shutdown log lines complete quickly ("all adapters disconnected", "Gateway stopped"), the "Exiting with code 1 …" line prints, but the **process does not terminate** — it joins the stuck non-daemon worker forever.

## Expected Behavior

After the graceful shutdown sequence has completed, the process should terminate promptly so the supervisor can start a fresh instance — even if a background worker thread is wedged.

## Actual Behavior

The process hangs in `Py_FinalizeEx` waiting on the stuck non-daemon thread. With supervisors that `SIGKILL` after a stop timeout (systemd `TimeoutStopSec`), the kill eventually arrives but the gateway is dead for that whole window; with supervisors that wait for clean exit, it can hang indefinitely. In all cases the api_server + cron are down for the duration.

### Evidence (representative log timeline, one occurrence)

```
14:08:54  gateway.run: ✓ discord disconnected (0.01s)
14:08:54  gateway.run: ✓ api_server disconnected (0.01s)
14:08:54  gateway.run: Shutdown phase: all adapters disconnected at +0.43s
14:08:54  gateway.run: Gateway stopped (total teardown 0.46s)
14:08:59  gateway.memory_monitor: [MEMORY] shutdown rss=739MB ... threads=23 ...
14:08:59  gateway.run: Exiting with code 1 (signal-initiated shutdown without restart request) ...
          --- process then lingers; same PID alive 2+ minutes later, api_server :8642 → connection refused,
              cron ticker stopped; cleared only by SIGKILL, after which a fresh gateway booted in ~12s ---
```

`threads=23` at shutdown; the gateway's own threads (cron ticker, etc.) are `daemon=True`, so the blocker is a non-daemon thread outside `run.py` — the `concurrent.futures` tool-worker pool, whose workers are non-daemon and are joined by the interpreter (and by `concurrent.futures.thread._python_exit`) at exit.

## Root Cause Analysis

`gateway/run.py` `main()`:

```python
success = asyncio.run(start_gateway(config))
if not success:
    sys.exit(1)        # ← SystemExit → Py_FinalizeEx joins all non-daemon threads
```

1. `SIGTERM` → graceful shutdown runs to completion inside `start_gateway()` and it returns `False` (signal-initiated, no restart requested).
2. `main()` calls `sys.exit(1)`.
3. `SystemExit` propagates; the interpreter begins finalization and **waits for all non-daemon threads to join**.
4. A `ThreadPoolExecutor` tool-worker is still executing Python/blocked in I/O with no timeout and never checks an exit flag → join never returns → process hangs.

There is **no `os._exit` / force-exit backstop** anywhere in `gateway/` — confirmed on the deployed release, the latest tagged release, and `main` (`HEAD`): the exit path is bare `sys.exit(1)` in all three. The teardown work is already done by the time we reach this line, so there is nothing left that *needs* a clean interpreter shutdown.

## Proposed Fix

After graceful shutdown has completed, force-exit instead of relying on a clean interpreter shutdown that can be blocked by a wedged worker:

```python
success = asyncio.run(start_gateway(config))
# Graceful shutdown already completed inside start_gateway() (adapters
# disconnected, sessions saved, cron stopped). A stuck non-daemon worker thread
# (e.g. a ThreadPoolExecutor tool/LLM call blocked with no timeout) must not be
# able to block interpreter finalization and hang the process with the
# api_server + cron already down. Flush logs, then hard-exit.
sys.stdout.flush()
sys.stderr.flush()
os._exit(0 if success else 1)
```

This is complementary to #14128's per-adapter disconnect timeout (defense in depth): the disconnect timeout keeps the *teardown* bounded, and the force-exit keeps *process termination* bounded regardless of which non-daemon thread is wedged. It also resolves the gateway manifestation of #27563.

(An equivalent, slightly gentler variant: spawn a watchdog thread that `os._exit`s if normal exit hasn't completed within N seconds — but since all cleanup is already done at this point, a direct `os._exit` is simplest and safe.)

## Affected Component

Gateway (`gateway/run.py`, process exit path).

## Hermes Version

Reproduced against v2026.5.29; vulnerable code path is byte-for-byte identical in v2026.6.19 (latest release) and on `main` (`HEAD`).

## Environment

- s6-supervised container deployment (Linux, Python 3.13). Also applies to systemd-supervised hosts (where it surfaces as #14128's "PID file race lost" after `TimeoutStopSec` `SIGKILL`).

items.title: Desktop: voice transcription times out (15s) on first faster-whisper model load
items.body:
## Problem
Voice transcription in the Hermes Desktop (Electron) app fails with:
> Voice transcription failed
> Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000 ms
## Root Cause
1. Desktop voice recording: **browser `getUserMedia` → Electron IPC → backend HTTP API** (`/api/audio/transcribe`), NOT the in-process CLI `voice_mode.py`.
2. `main.cjs`: `ensureBackend()` → `startHermes()` → `waitForHermes()` has **hard 15s timeout**.
3. `faster-whisper` first-time model load exceeds 15s — especially on Windows (symlink-less HF cache is slower).
4. Timeout fires before backend signals readiness.
## Evidence
`desktop.log`:
```
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes backend did not become ready: 
        Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms
```
Backend eventually starts on retry (`HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY port=...`).
`agent.log` — symlink warning on Windows:
```
huggingface_hub cache-system uses symlinks by default ... your machine does not support them
```
## Environment
- Windows 10, Hermes Desktop Electron
- STT: `local` (faster-whisper 1.2.1, model `base`)
- Config: `stt.enabled: true`, `stt.provider: local`
## Suggested Fix
1. **Increase backend readiness timeout** from 15s → 60s (`DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` / `waitForHermes`).
2. **Pre-warm STT model** on boot — transcribe a silent WAV to force model load before first real request.
3. **Progress indicator** in UI — poll `/api/health` with longer patience for voice activation, not hard-fail.
## Related Files
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` — `startHermes()`, `waitForHermes()`
- `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts` — `transcribeAudio()` → `POST /api/audio/transcribe`
- `tools/transcription_tools.py` — `transcribe_audio()` → `_transcribe_local()`
